newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Gilt vol flat as election fails to inspire.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Gilt vol flat as election fails to inspire.

text.p: Implied volatilities of gilt options on LIFFE were broadly steady on Friday in thin trade as investors shrugged off British money supply data earlier, traders said.
And with the British election campaign failing to spark any interest among investors, they expected the quiet tone to persist right up to around a week before the May 1 polling day.
Luke White, a broker at Fimat, said the main trade in gilts was a 110-00 strike straddle in May.
He said June at-the-money volatility was around 7.61 percent up from 7.58 percent at Thursday's close.
Another trader said September vol was at 7.4 to 7.7, also largely unchanged. "Today's been a real flat day, there's not a lot going on," he said.
June gilt futures were quoted at 109-28 at 1126 GMT, down 9/32 in the session.

British money supply and bank lending data earlier failed to garner any market interest, traders said. Provisional M4 money supply growth was 11.2 percent in March year-on-year versus an expected 11.0 percent and March major bank lending rose 5.551 billion sterling.
Traders said the market was turning a deaf ear to what they called a predictable election campaign.

"This is not an election that the UK markets have experienced before," said one trader at a British brokerage. "There's no difference between the major parties so if (the opposition Labour Party) win, nothing will seriously change." He added that a week before polling day things might start to get interesting.
"If you're looking for any signs of nerves you should look at the longer end and certainly on gilt option vol it hasn't really changed, it's just hanging around 7.5 to 7.75," he said.
